subject: Notice: Degraded interactive responses affecting live assistant (mitigations & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurelia.com>, Aurelia Platform Team <platform@aurelia.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Degraded interactive responses affecting live assistant (mitigations & next steps)

Hi Samir / Aurelia Platform Team,

Short version: between ~07:45 and 09:05 PDT today you may have seen intermittent slowdowns where the live assistant in your app returned responses in a staggered way (long pauses between token bursts). The visible symptom for end-users was the assistant appearing to stall for several hundred milliseconds at a time before continuing.

What we observed
- Scope: ~8% of requests hitting your production route experienced increased per-token latency (median per-token latency increased from ~20ms to ~220ms during the window).
- Impact: higher P95 response times for streaming connections; some UI retries were triggered by your client side timeouts.
- Affected endpoints: redwood.chat.stream and redwood.chat.respond (your integration uses streaming mode).

Immediate mitigations we applied on your behalf
1) Traffic routing: we moved a portion of your traffic (10%) to a warmer pool with a compatible model variant to reduce tail latency.
2) Fallback guidance: recommended temporary client-side change to switch to non-streaming (single-response) for known high-concurrency clients — this avoids perceived token-by-token stalls and returns the full response once completed.
3) Rate/concurrency suggestion: asked to cap concurrent streaming connections per node to 30 for 30 minutes while we stabilized.

Attachments: short log excerpt (aurelia_incident_log_excerpt.csv) showing request ids and timestamps.

What we are doing next (short timeline)
- Today: capture full traces + kernel telemetry, collect model-run metadata and scheduler traces.
- 24 hours: analyze batching/kernels to determine root cause (we suspect a scheduler interaction under bursty prefix patterns).
- 72 hours: provide a draft postmortem and permanent remediation plan.

Recommended actions for you (low-friction steps you can do now)
- If possible, toggle to non-streaming response mode for your most sensitive UI paths (saves the user experience while we fix the root cause).
- Reduce max_tokens to 512 for chat streams for the next 24 hours (some of the degraded requests were long-running).
- If you have tracing enabled, send us any correlation ids (x-request-id) we should prioritize.

We know this is disruptive — we’ve marked this high-priority and Diego is the primary engineer on the investigation. I’ll follow up with a more technical timeline within the hour.

Apologies for the disruption,

— Marissa

Subject: Follow-up & preliminary findings: interactive response delay incident (post-incident plan)

Hi Samir / Jordan / Aurelia team,

Thanks again for the patience while we completed the first pass analysis. This message summarizes what we’ve confirmed and the next steps; we’ll publish a formal postmortem doc to the Drive link shared earlier once the write-up is complete.

What we confirmed (preliminary)
- Root cause: a scheduler interaction combined with a rare kernel fallback on a subset of GPU instances under bursty prefix/cache patterns. In short, when many concurrent streaming requests shared similar prompt prefixes, our scheduler temporarily created less-efficient kernels for a small set of worker processes which increased per-token emission latency.
- Scope: ~7.9% of your streaming requests between 07:43 and 09:02 PDT showed the fallback behavior. No model weights were changed and there was no user-data loss or duplication. (Evelyn confirmed data integrity in storage and event logs.)
- Mitigation verified: the traffic routing we performed reduced exposure and your observed errors decreased within ~12 minutes of the routing adjustment.

Customer impact & SLA notes
- We agree the incident window for SLA calculations is 07:43:09 - 09:02:11 PDT on 2027-06-22. We’ll coordinate with your billing/contact to assess any credit per our SLA once you provide your correlated client-side window.

Temporary and long-term fixes
Short-term (already applied or safe to apply now):
- Optional: disable streaming for high-concurrency endpoints (client flag) — avoids visible stalling for end-users.
- Server-side: we have adjusted scheduling heuristics to avoid the identified kernel fallback pattern for the hot pool; this change has been rolled to 50% of nodes and is holding in canary.

Long-term (in progress):
- Scheduler fix: complete patch to routing heuristics to prevent the fallback condition (ETA 3 business days).
- Monitoring: add a high-resolution per-request kernel-selection metric to flag regressions earlier (ETA 1 week).
- SDK/Docs: Logan is drafting a short appendix for recommended streaming timeouts and retry logic for client SDKs.

Files attached: redwood_postmortem_draft_v1.pdf (internal draft), and an excerpted CSV with request ids we routed. Full trace bundle is available on request to the account security contact.

Next steps for your team
- If you want us to flip your production route to non-streaming while we complete the final fix, confirm and we’ll schedule a brief maintenance window tonight (low risk; no data migration needed).
- Send over any client-side request ids you want prioritized for next-level trace inspection.

We’ll update the Drive postmortem link with the final root-cause write-up and timeline for the permanent roll-forward. Please let me know if you prefer a short sync tomorrow with Diego and Evelyn to review technical details.

Thanks,

— Marissa
